title: As a developer, I can point an existing OpenAI SDK client at the provider by changing only the base URL and API key
As an AI-native user, I can have an agent switch to or away from this provider mid-workflow because it speaks the standard chat-completions API without provider-specific code changes
As an AI-native user, I can plug the provider into coding agents and agent frameworks through documented, first-party integration guides
As an AI-native user, I can have an agent enumerate the live model catalog programmatically via a documented GET /v1/models-style endpoint
As a developer, I can choose among a broad catalog of current open-weight model families (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, GPT-OSS and peers) on shared serverless endpoints
As an ml-engineer, I can get newly released open-weight models on the platform quickly after their public release
As a developer, I can rely on a documented deprecation policy with advance notice before a hosted model is removed
As an ml-engineer, I can see published tokens-per-second or latency numbers, benchmarks, or load-testing guides backing the provider's speed claims
As a developer, I can serve latency-sensitive workloads with fast time-to-first-token and high-throughput generation
As a developer, I can stream completions token by token over SSE for responsive user experiences
As an ml-engineer, I can benefit from prompt/prefix caching that reduces latency or cost on repeated context
As a developer, I can enforce structured outputs against a JSON schema (or grammar) so model responses parse reliably
As an AI-native user, I can rely on faithful function/tool calling — including parallel and multi-step tool use — so agent loops run on open models without breaking
As an ml-engineer, I can submit asynchronous batch inference jobs at a documented discount versus real-time pricing
As an ml-engineer, I can fine-tune a supported base model on my own data and serve the result on the same platform
As an ml-engineer, I can upload and serve my own custom model weights or LoRA adapters
As an ml-engineer, I can deploy a model on dedicated GPU capacity with autoscaling so my traffic is isolated from the shared serverless pool
As a founder, I can see public per-token prices for every hosted model without talking to sales
As a developer, I can read documented rate limits and how they scale across usage tiers before I hit them in production
As a founder, I can set spending caps or budget alerts so a runaway workload cannot generate an unbounded bill
As a founder, I can check a public status page with incident history before betting production traffic on the platform
As a founder, I can get a stated availability SLA on paid or enterprise tiers
As a developer, I can call vision, audio, or image-generation models beyond text chat on the same platform
As a developer, I can generate embeddings (and rerank results) for retrieval pipelines without a second vendor
